sections.prepared_remarks: Apple reporting Q2 revenue of $95.4 billion, up 5 percent year over year. iPhone revenue of $61.6 billion, with June iPhone cycle showing strong momentum as consumers await new models in September. Services revenue of $26.3 billion, up 14 percent, a new September quarter record. Mac revenue of $7.8 billion driven by M4 MacBook Air adoption in education and enterprise. iPad revenue of $7.2 billion with new iPad Pro M4 driving upgrade cycle. Greater China revenue $16.6 billion, down modestly due to competitive pressure and macroeconomic headwinds, though customer survey data showsimproving brand perception scores. Total active installed base now over 2.25 billion devices. Our AI strategy is resonating: Apple Intelligence adoption rates are meaningfully ahead of where we saw Siri adoption in earlier cycles. We are rolling out expanded language support and additional markets throughout fiscal 2025.
sections.financial_highlights: EPS $2.33, gross margin 47.3 percent, up 60 basis points year over year. We returned $28 billion to shareholders. Services margins hit a new all-time high of 75.2 percent. We are targeting operating leverage through disciplined cost management while increasing AI infrastructure investment. R&D spending grew 12 percent year over year. Our data center expansion is on schedule to support on-device and cloud-based AI workloads. We continue to generate substantial free cash flow — $29 billion this quarter — and maintain a strong balance sheet with $68 billion in cash. Currency headwinds reduced revenue by approximately 100 basis points. On a constant currency basis, revenue would have grown 6 percent year over year.
sections.qanda_session:
David Vogt: Tim, the China situation — you mentioned stabilizing perception scores. Can you give us a sense for whether that is a product cycle story or more about competitive positioning versus Huawei and local brands? And does the Apple Intelligence roadmap in China require any special arrangements with local cloud providers?

Tim Cook: David, on China, I'll say a few things. First, we are very committed to the China market and proud of our 25-year presence there. The product cycle matters but so does the ecosystem lock-in and privacy positioning. People in China trust Apple with their data in a way they don't trust others. On AI regulations — we are working constructively with the relevant authorities and we'll comply with local requirements. We think we have a pathway that respects both the regulations and our architecture, where certain AI processing goes through Apple-controlled infrastructure.

Krish Sankar: Luca, you mentioned the September quarter outlook implies a meaningful acceleration from the June quarter. Can you help us size the iPhone 17 ramp contribution versus Services continuing momentum? And is there any initial guidance for Apple Intelligence monetization — is this a services revenue driver in fiscal 2025 or more of a product catalyst?

Luca Maestri: Krish, on the September quarter, the iPhone lineup is refreshed with a full year of AI integration across the lineup. We expect meaningful iPhone revenue acceleration driven by the cycle and also some favorable year-over-year compares. Services continues at its current trajectory — mid-teens growth — driven by advertising, cloud, and App Store. On AI monetization: you'll see it in Services this year through things like enhanced Siri capabilities in the App Store, but we are not breaking it out as a separate line item. The bigger Services AI revenue tailwinds come in fiscal 2026 as developer integrations and subscription AI features scale up.
sections.forward_outlook: Tim Cook: We are entering the most exciting product lineup in Apple's history. I'm not going to preview specifics, but I will say that we have never had a stronger product pipeline. Apple Silicon is extending our lead. Our custom modem development remains on track. The spatial computing category we created with Vision Pro will expand to entirely new price points. We are the only company with seamless continuity across iPhone, Mac, Watch, iPad, and Vision — and Intelligence makes this ecosystem stickier than ever. We are confident in our ability to grow revenue and generate industry-leading returns for shareholders.
